structure.title: Ratios in the Real World
structure.objective: Students use ratio language to describe relationships between quantities and solve unit-rate problems from real contexts.
steps: Warm-up: identify three ratios in the classroom (5 min)
Guided practice from OpenStax Prealgebra Ch. 5 exercise set
Partner task: price-per-unit comparison at a real store flyer
Exit check: two unit-rate problems, self-scored against rubric

differentiation.support: Provide a ratio-table graphic organizer; use whole-number quantities only.
differentiation.extension: Introduce three-quantity ratios and part:part:whole reasoning.

structure.title: Author's Argument Deep Read
structure.objective: Students trace and evaluate an author's argument, citing strong textual evidence.
steps: First read: annotate claims vs. evidence (public-domain text from library)
Second read: map the argument structure in pairs
Written response: evaluate whether the evidence supports the claim
Peer review against the rubric

differentiation.support: Sentence starters for claims/evidence; chunked text.
differentiation.extension: Compare two authors' arguments on the same subject.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Cites evidence loosely tied to claim

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Evaluates sufficiency and bias of evidence

structure.title: Matter and Its Interactions Lab
structure.objective: Students develop a model to describe how particle arrangement changes with state of matter.
steps: Phenomenon hook: condensation on a cold glass
Investigation in station groups; record observations
Model drawing: particle diagrams across three states
CER write-up: Claim, Evidence, Reasoning

differentiation.support: Pre-drawn particle diagram frames to annotate.
differentiation.extension: Add energy transfer arrows and explain anomalies (evaporative cooling).

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Model predicts a new scenario correctly

structure.title: Primary Source Investigation: My City
structure.objective: Students corroborate multiple primary sources to construct an account of a local historical event.
steps: Select an event from the local history source set (Library of Congress / DPLA)
Source analysis sheets: author, audience, purpose, perspective
Corroboration matrix across 3+ sources
Final product: exhibit panel, podcast segment, or short essay

differentiation.extension: Locate one additional source independently and assess reliability.

structure.title: Interpretive Listening Circle
structure.objective: Students interpret an authentic audio text and sustain a target-language discussion.
steps: Two listens of an authentic clip with structured note frames
Small-group meaning negotiation in target language
Whole-class discussion with sentence frames
Self-assessment against can-do statements

differentiation.support: Transcript available on second listen; glossary of 8 key terms.
differentiation.extension: No transcript; students summarize register and tone.

structure.title: Rhythm Patterns to Composition
structure.objective: Students create and notate a four-measure rhythm composition and perform it.
steps: Echo-clap warm-up with quarter/eighth patterns
Pattern bank building on rhythm cards
Compose four measures; notate with icon or standard notation
Perform for a partner; partner claps it back from notation

differentiation.extension: Add rests and a second voice (body percussion ostinato).
